facts.subject: Forgotten Engine
facts.statement: Completing the Forgotten Engine mission removes the radiation border and opens the new Update 1 regions.

facts.subject: Expanded map
facts.statement: Update 1 adds unlockable regions, abandoned bases, antennas, caves, resource sites, factory space, foundables, dialogue, audiologs, and datapads; the official notes do not publish a numerical area increase.

facts.subject: Powerium
facts.statement: Powerium deposits require an Oil Extractor; the extracted product flows through the Refinery. SRDB names the recipe output item Crude Oil, so deposit identity and item identity must remain separate.
facts.notes: Official Update 1 prose establishes the Powerium -> Oil Extractor -> Refinery chain; SRDB supplies the exact entity IDs.

facts.subject: Goethite
facts.statement: Goethite deposits require a Laser Drill and the extracted ore is refined through the Pyro Forge.

facts.subject: Update 1 production content
facts.statement: Creepy Jar advertised more than 40 new items and recipes in Update 1 but did not enumerate all numerical rates; use the versioned SRDB recipe snapshot for exact current data.

facts.subject: Development Station
facts.statement: The Development Station is placed inside a Habitat and unlocks improved building versions through corporation, material, reputation, and tracked-task requirements represented separately from recipe research.
facts.evidence_locator: Development upgrade groups, requirements, tasks, and rewards

facts.subject: Higher-tier buildings
facts.statement: The advertised higher-tier set includes Compounder v.2, Fabricator v.2, Furnace v.2, Ore Excavator v.2, Orbital Cargo Launcher v.2, and Constructorizer v.2; official prose also identifies Large Personal Storage and Large Habitat among Development Station rewards.
facts.evidence_locator: New higher tier buildings and Development Station sections

facts.subject: Recycler
facts.statement: The Recycler is a Habitat-interior station that converts items into Basic Building Materials and/or Intermediate Building Materials; specific yields must come from recipe data rather than this prose rule.

facts.subject: Zipline
facts.statement: Players build a Zipline graph from Zipline Poles and can choose either direction along a track for rapid traversal; unlike Drone Rails, the Zipline carries the player rather than resources.

facts.subject: Passive wildlife
facts.statement: Update 1 adds Vulpir, Coralion, and Skylisk as generally shy wildlife and adds related consumable content.

facts.subject: Update 1 migration
facts.statement: Update 1 reset every corporation to level 1 and restored prior progression as Data Points that could be redistributed in the Corporate Terminal.

facts.subject: Pre-Update 1 buildings
facts.statement: Buildings already unlocked and placed before Update 1 remained operational, but the 0.2.0 launch initially required the relevant Corporate Terminal or Development Station unlock before they could be built again.

facts.subject: Pre-Update 1 buildings
facts.statement: From hotfix 0.2.2, loading a pre-Update 1 save automatically unlocks previously unlocked or built buildings in the Development Station.

facts.subject: Walkway and Dash
facts.statement: Mechanics previously available at the start moved behind corporation levels: Extendable Walkway to Moon Energy level 4 and Dash to Griffits Blue level 3.

facts.subject: UPP-7 Pistol
facts.statement: The pistol is no longer a corporation-level reward; it is crafted through the Equipment Upgrade Station with other weapons.

facts.subject: Death
facts.statement: Death drops all weapons the player is carrying, explicitly including the pistol; corpse recovery and inventory-loss questions should therefore model weapons as losable inventory.

facts.subject: Teleporter
facts.statement: The Teleporter moved from a Forgotten Engine reward to Clever Robotics level 9; launching the Forgotten Engine is no longer required to unlock it.
facts.evidence_locator: Teleporter is now a Corporation Reward

facts.subject: Quartz
facts.statement: Quartz is no longer a building construction material; Quartz Ore instead participates in Development Station progression.
facts.evidence_locator: Quartz is no longer a Building Material

facts.subject: Legacy Quartz Building Material
facts.statement: Quartz already spent on buildings was refunded as Quartz Ore; remaining legacy Quartz Building Material cannot build but can be recycled losslessly into Quartz Ore.
facts.evidence_locator: Quartz is no longer a Building Material

facts.subject: Former Quartz-cost buildings
facts.statement: Buildings that formerly consumed Quartz Building Material now consume Base Core overheat capacity instead.
facts.evidence_locator: Quartz is no longer a Building Material

facts.subject: Cargo Dispatcher and Receiver
facts.statement: Cargo links are strictly one Dispatcher to one selected Receiver; pre-Update 1 connections must be manually reconnected.

facts.subject: Cargo Dispatcher
facts.statement: Manual parcel sizing was removed; the Dispatcher automatically packs and sends material to its paired Receiver every 20 seconds.

facts.subject: Duplicate blueprints
facts.statement: Picking up a blueprint already found produces a Data Points item instead of adding another duplicate blueprint entry.

facts.subject: Forgotten Engine blueprints
facts.statement: Blueprints previously located in the Forgotten Engine moved to other locations in Update 1.

facts.subject: Nanofibre recipe
facts.statement: Nanofibre gained Wolfram Wire as a third recipe input.

facts.subject: Pressure Tank recipe
facts.statement: Pressure Tank no longer requires Titanium Housing.

facts.subject: Condenser recipe
facts.statement: Condenser no longer requires Synthetic Resin.

facts.subject: Superconductor recipe
facts.statement: Superconductor uses Synthetic Resin where the prior recipe used Ceramics.

facts.subject: Recipe
facts.statement: A recipe is modeled by producer building associations, input items and quantities, output item and quantity, cycle duration, item level, and optional material/Data Point research requirements; recipe outputs remain a separate relation for future multi-output support.

facts.subject: Recipe Station
facts.statement: Recipe research costs are distinct from corporation reputation, player XP, and Development Station upgrades; they can include items, blueprints, and Data Points.

facts.subject: Analyzing Station
facts.statement: Analyzable items yield item-specific Data Point values; these are stored separately from export reputation and player XP.

facts.subject: Orbital Cargo Launcher exports
facts.statement: Export offers are corporation- and corporation-level-specific item values; a zero value is not an offer and different levels can value the same item differently.

facts.subject: Player XP
facts.statement: Player XP sources are classified as Movement, Combat, or Survival actions and must not be conflated with Data Points or corporation reputation.

facts.subject: Building power_raw
facts.statement: SRDB uses positive raw power values for generation and negative raw values for consumption. Derived generation and demand columns retain the untouched raw value and should be validated against the current game before high-stakes optimization.

facts.subject: Building temperature_raw
facts.statement: SRDB temperature values appear to encode positive capacity load and negative capacity contribution, but descriptions and numbers are not uniformly self-consistent. Preserve temperature_raw and treat derived load/bonus values as provisional.

facts.subject: Drone Rails
facts.statement: Drone logistics form a directed socket graph with rail tiers, poles, junctions, modulators, roundabouts, producer/consumer requests, storage behavior, and power conduction; socket groups and counts must be retained rather than collapsed to a single connector count.

facts.subject: Loot locations
facts.statement: Map loot is represented by markers linked to loot tables whose entries contain item, probability, minimum, and maximum fields; probability semantics remain unvalidated and must not yet drive expected-value models.

facts.subject: NPC spawn presets
facts.statement: NPC spawn markers retain raw AI type identifiers, burst-preset settings, custom archetype names, and spawn-count values; display-name mapping and combat formulas require separate validation.

facts.subject: Coordinates
facts.statement: SRDB map coordinates are preserved in their source coordinate space. They must not be mixed with raw game-world or other map coordinate systems until a transform is verified.
facts.evidence_locator: Map marker and radiation polygon coordinates

facts.subject: Ruptura timer
facts.statement: The SRDB timer bundle models a 54-minute cycle: Burning 30 seconds, Cooling 60 seconds, Stabilizing 600 seconds, and Stable 2,550 seconds. This is community-tool logic tied to the SRDB 2.3.4 capture, not an official formula guarantee.

facts.subject: Post-Ruptura regeneration
facts.statement: Official Update 1 prose describes foliage regrowth and water replenishment after the Ruptura fire wave; exact respawn timing and formulas are not published.

facts.subject: Structural stability
facts.statement: Supported platforms, foundations, pillars, Habitats, Airlocks, snapping relationships, and dependent deconstruction form a structural dependency system; building placement is not only a material-cost check.
facts.evidence_locator: Official Base Building Basics Part 2 and Update 1 hotfix lineage

facts.subject: Platform stability
facts.statement: Hotfix 0.2.5 reduced Platform stability cost; scenarios that depend on exact stability limits must distinguish pre-0.2.5 from 0.2.5-and-later Update 1 builds.

facts.subject: Weapon statistics
facts.statement: Current SRDB weapon pages still identify their numerical statistics as Play Test 2 data. Preserve and query them, but do not claim they are verified Update 1 balance without in-game confirmation.

facts.subject: Weapon modifications
facts.statement: Weapon modifications are linked to a weapon and slot, carry a currency cost, and apply one or more named attribute modifiers; raw modifier names and values are retained because operator semantics require validation.

facts.subject: LEM modules
facts.statement: LEM items are separated into Combat, Movement, and Survival categories; their description text encodes the effect while equip-slot, stacking, and exact operator behavior require separate validation.

facts.subject: Supported party size
facts.statement: StarRupture officially supports online co-op for up to four players; host, client, and dedicated-server synchronization fixes should be stored as historical behavior rather than generalized into new design rules.

facts.subject: Hidden and prototype entities
facts.statement: The SRDB search index exposes hidden, test, prototype, non-deconstructible, foundation, and internal variants. Preserve them with raw IDs and flags, but player-facing scenario defaults must exclude hidden or unassigned content unless explicitly requested.
facts.evidence_locator: Full search index and hidden building detail pages

facts.subject: discovered field
facts.statement: The SRDB discovered field is provenance-like and not a reliable gameplay-availability flag; even central Update 1 entities can retain test labels. Availability must combine source flags, producer associations, unlocks, and explicit evidence.

facts.subject: Source versioning
facts.statement: SRDB 2.3.4 was updated July 10, 2026 but declares its game data as Update 1, internal game version 35118973, dated April 9, 2026. The source snapshot date and claimed game-data build are separate version axes.
facts.evidence_locator: Header game-data marker and footer SRDB version

facts.subject: Patch-note interpretation
facts.statement: A patch-note bug fix proves a historical behavior and an intended correction but does not by itself define every underlying mechanic or formula; bugfix_behavior and design_delta assertions remain distinct.
